title: Man killed by RCMP near Vegreville identified
article: RCMP shot and killed a 43-year-old man Wednesday evening during a confrontation at a home north of Vegreville.
The shooting is under investigation by the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team.

ASIRT executive director Clif Purvis said police were first called to the property 25 kilometres northeast of Lavoy at about 2:10 p.m. regarding a report of "trouble" with a man, who was potentially armed. Three uniformed officers responded to the call and arrived at the scene by 3:30 p.m.
A police negotiator and the RCMP's special Emergency Response Team were en route when the shooting occurred at 5 p.m.
The dead man's name is not yet being released by officials, but neighbours in the area identified the man as Russell Skoropad.
Purvis said he could not comment on what happened at the home between the time police arrived and when the shooting occurred, nor could he elaborate on the circumstances that led to the shooting.

"Certainly that's really the focus of our investigation," he said. "We'll conduct a thorough, independent investigation, and we'll try to discover why the shot was fired and whether or not it was justified and lawful in the end."
A shotgun was found at the scene.
Purvis said the officer who shot the man is an 11-year veteran of the RCMP. The officers with him have been on the force for eight years and two years, respectively.
The 43-year-old man was shot once. Purvis said emergency medical treatment was provided after the shooting, but the man died at the scene.

Three adult members of the man's family were also at the scene, and Purvis said witnesses are still being interviewed. He said investigators are still looking at whether the people were eyewitnesses or were simply in the area at the time.

Neighbour Rick Wasylciw was at home when he heard a gunshot at the neighbour's property. He said Skoropad had been living in a motorhome on his mother's property for about a year or two. Two of Skoropad's brothers - one younger and one older - lived inside the home with their mother.

He described Skoropad as a decent man who had recently landed a new job with the county clearing brush. When Wasylciw was outside working on his truck, Skoropad would stop by to help, even without being asked.
"When I was doing work out there he was the first one to climb in and give me a hand," he said. "I can't say a bad thing about him."
Purvis said an autopsy was scheduled for Thursday.
He did not know whether the man was previously known to police.
Spokeswoman Doris Stapleton said RCMP will not comment since the case is in the hands of ASIRT investigators.
Vegreville Mayor Richard N. Coleman said Thursday afternoon he hadn't heard about the shooting.
On July 12, 2008, Vegreville RCMP shot and killed an armed, schizophrenic man who had driven to the local RCMP detachment with a sawed-off, 12-gauge shotgun.

Witnesses in that case said police told the man to drop the shotgun up to 20 times, but he was shot after he raised the gun and pointed it at one of the officers. It was described at the time as an apparent attempt at "suicide by cop," and ASIRT later concluded the shooting had been justified.
